source_refs.note: Exercise 10.1, Question 3: book page 278 (Q1-Q24). The book prints no answers for Exercise 10.1.

blocks.explanation:
A square of \(\tan x\) is given: isolate \(\tan^{2}x\) and take the square root with \(\pm\).
This gives two basic equations \(\tan x = \pm\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\).
Plan: solve each in \([0, 2\pi]\); then use the period \(\pi\) of tangent.
steps:
Given: \(3\tan^{2}x = 1\).
To find: principal solutions and general solution.
Method: isolate \(\tan^{2}x\), take the square root (two signs), solve the two basic equations; the period of \(\tan x\) is \(\pi\).

Isolate and take the square root
\[\tan^{2}x = \dfrac{1}{3}\]
\[\tan x = \pm\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\]
Why: divide by 3; a square root always has two signs.

Reference angle
\[\tan\alpha = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\]
\[\alpha = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\]
Why: \(\tan\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) from the table.

When \(\tan x = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\)
Tangent is positive, so \(x\) is in quadrant I or III:
\[x = \dfrac{\pi}{6}\]
\[x = \pi + \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{7\pi}{6}\]
Why: tangent is positive in quadrants I and III.

When \(\tan x = -\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\)
Tangent is negative, so \(x\) is in quadrant II or IV:
\[x = \pi - \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{5\pi}{6}\]
\[x = 2\pi - \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{11\pi}{6}\]
Why: tangent is negative in quadrants II and IV.

General solution
The period of \(\tan x\) is \(\pi\). Since \(\frac{7\pi}{6} = \frac{\pi}{6} + \pi\) and \(\frac{11\pi}{6} = \frac{5\pi}{6} + \pi\), two families cover all four principal solutions:
\[\left\{\dfrac{\pi}{6} + n\pi\right\}\]
\[\cup \left\{\dfrac{5\pi}{6} + n\pi\right\},\ n \in \mathbb{Z}\]
Why: tangent repeats every \(\pi\), so we add \(n\pi\), not \(2n\pi\).

Check
\[\tan^{2}\dfrac{\pi}{6} = \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)^{2} = \dfrac{1}{3}\]
\[3 \cdot \dfrac{1}{3} = 1\]
Why: at \(\frac{5\pi}{6}, \frac{7\pi}{6}, \frac{11\pi}{6}\) the value of \(\tan x\) is \(\pm\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\) as well, so \(\tan^{2}x = \frac{1}{3}\) in every case.
blocks.final_answer: Principal solutions in \([0, 2\pi]\): \(x = \frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{5\pi}{6}, \frac{7\pi}{6}, \frac{11\pi}{6}\). General solution: \(\left\{\frac{\pi}{6} + n\pi\right\}\) \(\cup\) \(\left\{\frac{5\pi}{6} + n\pi\right\}\), \(n \in \mathbb{Z}\). (Equivalently, with period \(2\pi\): the four sets \(\frac{\pi}{6}, \frac{5\pi}{6}, \frac{7\pi}{6}, \frac{11\pi}{6}\), each \(+ 2n\pi\).)

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: The textbook prints no answers for Exercise 10.1. Every answer on this page is ours: worked out step by step, checked independently with a computer algebra system (sympy) and compared with a solution book. As in the book's examples, we give the principal solutions in \([0, 2\pi]\) and the general solution as a union of sets.
